meta.title: Routing strategy: partner with RouteSprout now, and buy only on conditional terms
meta.subtitle: Board pre-read for the March 2027 meeting · Should Atlas buy RouteSprout in 2027, and on what terms, rather than build or partner?
meta.purpose: Decide whether to buy RouteSprout in 2027, and on what terms, rather than build or partner
meta.confidentiality: Synthetic benchmark data · figures from the briefing pack or labelled team assumptions · $ in millions unless stated

inputs.label: Atlas FieldOps briefing pack (synthetic benchmark data)

storyline.governing_thought: Do not buy RouteSprout on the proposed terms in 2027: partner now, and keep a conditional option to buy later at no more than $8.5M upfront

exec_summary.text: Neither acquisition path stays inside the cash limits once 18 months of operating losses are counted

sub_points.text: Path A needs $22.0M against a $15.0M ceiling; Path B fits at signing but falls to $7.2M–8.2M, below the $9.0M floor
Nothing in the plan funds the $7.0M earnout due in 2029

exec_summary.text: The value case is overstated, and buying takes more than 15 years to pay back

sub_points.text: $18.0M is 3.75 times recognized ARR, not the sellers' 2.5 times bookings
The $2.4M cross-sell is ARR, not EBITDA: net it adds about $0.1M a year, and loses $1.2M in the low case

exec_summary.text: Customer and execution risk is high and is not priced into the deal case

sub_points.text: Churn rose from 12% to 21%, 41 accounts hold 58% of ARR and 30% of integration is unscoped, yet sellers assume 100% renewal

exec_summary.text: Only the partnership passes all four board criteria in 2027; building is affordable but late

sub_points.text: At most $1.2M at risk, live this summer, no migration, and it out-earns ownership below about $3.5M of ARR

exec_summary.text: Buying stays possible, but only on conditional terms tested at a Q1 2028 gate

sub_points.text: Partner now with first refusal; buy later for at most $8.5M upfront plus up to $9.5M if earned
Buy only if six thresholds clear; integrate via the API and pay nothing that breaks the cash floor

next_steps.action: Decline the $18.0M all-cash proposal (Path A) and the staged deal as structured (Path B)
Approve and sign the two-year RouteSprout partnership with the protections on p. 14
Run preliminary diligence: QoE, customer cohorts, integration scoping, key-person review
Negotiate the conditional term sheet: at most $8.5M upfront, up to $9.5M earned, set walk-away
Decide at the gate: buy only if all six thresholds are met

lead_message.text: Our starting hypothesis, a staged purchase of RouteSprout in 2027, fails four of five tests; customer protection is unproven

slides.rationale: Hypothesis tested against five conditions -> comparison table with a verdict column

columns: What would have to be true

cells.text: Cash stays at or above the $9.0M floor through 2028, and the earnout can be funded
Path B leaves $0.5M of headroom at signing, then falls to $7.2M–8.2M by end-2028; the $7.0M earnout has no funding source
The price rests on verified recurring revenue
3.75 times recognized ARR, not 2.5 times; bookings include multi-year value and pilots; no quality-of-earnings (QoE) review
Positive incremental contribution within a reasonable horizon
+$0.07M (base) or −$1.21M (low) a year while integration support runs; payback over 15 years
Renewals and 99.7% uptime survive integration
Churn rose from 12% to 21%, the case assumes 100% renewal, an early interface swap risks churn, and no cohort data exists
Better on cash, payback, continuity and execution
The partnership earns more below about $3.5M of routing ARR and risks at most $1.2M; building is slower but cheaper

lead_message.text: RouteSprout's churn is rising and its revenue is concentrated, yet the sellers' case assumes every account renews

sidebar.header: What this means for the deal
bullets: **Concentration magnifies churn:** losing a handful of the 41 large accounts would wipe out a year of cross-sell
**People drive renewals:** interviews found account managers, not routing features, drive renewal decisions, so RouteSprout's account managers matter as much as its code
**Interface timing:** the product VP warns that replacing RouteSprout's interface before large customers renew could add churn
**No cohort data:** we cannot tell whether churn sits in small or large accounts; this is the first diligence item

panels.header: Logo churn rose from 12% to 21% in two years; the sellers' case assumes none
58% of ARR sits in 41 accounts, about $68K each against $7.5K for the other 269

lead_message.text: The synergy, retention and integration claims rest on correlations and untested plans, not on evidence of cause

lead_message.text: Sign the partnership on terms that cap cost, protect uptime and stop a competitor from capturing RouteSprout

slides.rationale: Two groups of contract terms -> text columns, protection emphasized

columns.header: Commercial terms cap the cost and protect uptime
detail: **Scope and price (as offered):** non-exclusive routing API with a $1.2M two-year minimum; gross profit splits 55% to Atlas and 45% to RouteSprout
**Ask, credit the minimum:** count minimum payments against RouteSprout's 45% share, which cuts the $1.36M break-even and the $1.2M maximum loss
**Service level:** at least 99.7% quarterly uptime, with service credits passed back to Atlas to match the credits Atlas owes its large customers
**Ask, segment exclusivity:** exclusivity in utilities and repair contractors, Atlas's core segments; negotiate for it, but do not make it a condition

columns.header: Protection terms stop a competitor capturing RouteSprout
detail: **Change of control:** right of first refusal on any sale of RouteSprout, plus a right to terminate if a competitor buys it; the founders want to sell, so this is the key protection
**Pre-agreed purchase option:** attach the conditional term sheet (p. 15), exercisable at the Q1 2028 gate, with partnership fees credited against the price
**Information rights:** customer-level churn cohorts, the ARR schedule and pipeline data, which double as diligence evidence
**Continuity and roadmap:** source-code escrow and data portability in case RouteSprout fails (EBITDA −$1.0M); share only interface-level roadmap, through a clean team
**Why walk away without them:** the roadmap risk would then outweigh the speed benefit

slides.so_what: Walk away if RouteSprout refuses first-refusal or change-of-control terms; reopen the build

slides.so_what: Early trigger: if a rival bidder emerges, use first refusal only once items 1, 2 and 5 clear

lead_message.text: In March, approve the partnership, fund diligence and set walk-away terms; decide on buying at a Q1 2028 gate

slides.rationale: Decisions asked now, then the sequence after approval -> two text columns

detail: **Decline** the $18.0M all-cash proposal (Path A) and the staged deal as structured (Path B)
**Approve** the two-year RouteSprout partnership (at most $1.2M minimum) with the protections on p. 14
**Approve preliminary diligence:** QoE, customer cohorts, integration scoping and key-person review; the CFO sizes the budget, which the pack does not give
**Mandate** negotiation of the conditional term sheet: at most $8.5M upfront and up to $9.5M earned, with a set walk-away
**Defer** the internal build, and revisit it at the gate if the partnership underperforms
**Apr–Jun 2027:** sign the partnership; run diligence in parallel and negotiate the conditional term sheet
**Summer 2027:** routing goes live with the enterprise prospects that asked for it; track attach and ARR
**Q3–Q4 2027:** QoE and cohort results arrive; watch renewal outcomes for RouteSprout's 41 large accounts
**Q1 2028 gate:** buy if all six thresholds are met (p. 16); otherwise continue the partnership, or start the build if demand is proven but the partner falls short
**Any time:** if a competing bid emerges, apply the early trigger (p. 16)

slides.so_what: Our reading: partnering in 2027, then buying in 2028, counts as one routing strategy

units.text: Do not buy RouteSprout on the proposed terms in 2027; partner now and keep a conditional option to buy later at no more than $8.5M upfront
Reject the $18.0M all-cash deal (Path A) and the staged deal as structured (Path B)
Sign a two-year RouteSprout partnership ($1.2M minimum, live summer 2027) with a right of first refusal and a pre-agreed conditional purchase option
Exercise the purchase option at a Q1 2028 gate only if six evidence thresholds are met
Path A needs $22.0M against a $15.0M ceiling ($24.0M − $9.0M); leaves $2.0M before operating losses
Path B fits at signing ($14.5M, $0.5M headroom) but 18 months of operating drag takes cash to $7.2–8.2M, below the $9.0M floor
Nothing funds the $7.0M earnout due in 2029; base-case run-rate contribution of $0.92M/yr needs about 7.6 years
30% of integration unscoped; every $1 overrun is $1 below the floor; if integration-era support counts toward the $4.0M cap, A = $5.3M and B = $4.8M breach it
Uptime service credits (99.7%) are unquantified and only run one way
Any acquisition must leave room for 18 months of losses, a contingency on unscoped work and an earnout that does not have to be paid in cash
$18.0M is 3.75x recognized ARR, 50% above the sellers' 2.5x of bookings; bookings include multi-year contract value and pilots; no QoE; ARR unverified
Path B total including the full earnout is also $18.0M (3.75x): structure moves timing, not amount
Cross-sell $2.4M is ARR not EBITDA; contribution +$0.07M base / −$1.21M low in integration era; +$0.92M / −$0.36M after support ends
About $1.0M of RouteSprout ARR at risk each year at 21% churn (logo churn as proxy), not in the base numbers
Payback: A ≈24 years / never; B ≈16 (23 with earnout) / never; C ≈1.1 years, break-even $1.36M, max loss $1.2M; D ≈5.3 years after launch
Simple undiscounted payback; no precise DCF from unavailable inputs; partner low end more likely
Logo churn rose from 12% to 21%; 58% of ARR in 41 accounts; sellers assume 100% renewal
Account managers drive renewals; replacing the interface before large renewals risks churn; no cohort data, first diligence item
Synergy and retention claims rest on correlation (95% vs 78% renewal confounded; cited deals twice as large); no retention uplift credited, $2.4M not underwritten
Integrate through the API first; scope 100% of the work and price contingency before signing
Signed 24-month retention agreements for key engineers and account managers are a condition of the deal
Only the partnership passes all four board criteria in 2027; the build is the fallback, not the first move
Partnership earns more than ownership below about $3.5M of routing ARR ($3.47M; $2.78M after support ends); capital excluded widens the lead
Partner-sold routing at the same 80% margin; $1.2M minimum fixed and not recoupable
Building is affordable ($3.4M) but cannot ship before late 2028; misses renewal cycles; displaces the compliance upgrade; $1.3M ARR treated as 2029 run-rate
Partnership terms: ask to credit the minimum, 99.7% SLA with credits passed back, information rights, segment exclusivity ask, escrow and data portability, clean team
Walk away from the partnership if RouteSprout refuses first refusal or change-of-control protection; reopen the build

Conditional purchase: at most $8.5M upfront (≈1.8x verified ARR), cut ≈1.8x per ARR shortfall; earnout up to $9.5M within $18.0M on four tests; paid only above floor plus buffer, deferred or in equity
API plus SSO first; no interface replacement or record migration before large-account renewals; scoped budget ≤ $4.0M including support
Walk away if sellers demand more than $8.5M upfront or all cash; keep the partnership
Upfront ceiling derivation: 15.0 − 4.0 − 2.3 = 8.7 → 8.5; drops $1-for-$1 for uncredited fees or budget above cap; $0.2M buffer thin

Six thresholds: QoE ARR ≥ $4.8M; churn toward 12% and stable top-41; signed demand ≥ $1.36M (≈$2.3M to cover losses); EBITDA breakeven needs ≈$1.06M; scoped budget ≤ $4.0M; retention agreements and ≤ $8.5M upfront
Early trigger: if a competing buyer emerges, use ROFR on pre-agreed terms only if items 1, 2 and 5 have cleared
Five March 2027 decisions and the sequence to the Q1 2028 gate; CFO sizes the diligence budget
Partnering in 2027 then buying in 2028 counts as one routing strategy; if the board disagrees the gate is partnership vs build only
Five risks with mitigations and residual exposure; cash downside capped at $1.2M
Starting hypothesis (staged purchase in 2027) fails four of five tests; customer protection unproven; revised answer partner now, buy as an option
Assumptions register (close timing, EBITDA flat, linear ramp, support duration, partner economics, no synergies)
Calculation trail for every figure

check.notes: Read unit by unit against the slides: every critical unit is on a main-deck slide with the source's numbers, conditions and option ranking (partner > conditional buy > build fallback > A/B rejected). No corrections: every number in the source reproduces from the pack or from its stated assumptions. Wording changes only: slide 3 title names the unproven test (customer protection) instead of 'the fifth', since test 5 is itself a Fail; slide 7 title shortened with the low case in brackets; British spellings made American.
